messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: dedicated pool 'dedicated-eu3-hotshot' p99 latency spike > 4.8s, p95 > 1.2s. Paging oncall.
oncall-eng: Ack. Investigating now. Paging SRE.
sre-alex: Looking at metrics — queue depth spiked to ~14k for the hotshot pool. Autoscaler requested scales but many new workers stuck in WARMUP. KV-cache hit rate dropped to 42%.
eng-runtime-lee: Confirmed: warmup handshakes are backing up; a lot of workers stuck in TIMED_WAIT during model load. Container logs show long model init (quantized weights) and high disk io.
oncall-eng: Any customer-visible errors or 5xxs?
support-maya: No 5xxs recorded. ~87 customer requests saw >10s latency in last 5m. 3 streaming tickets opened reporting stalls/aborts.
ops-rita: Starting emergency reroute: deprioritizing non-urgent routes and shifting embeddings/rerank traffic off hotshot pool.
eng-runtime-lee: Executed routing change: `route set --pool dedicated-eu3-hotshot --weight 0.6` and `route bump --service embeddings --fallback=dedicated-eu3-standard` — rolling now.
sre-alex: Autoscaler logs: scale requested but handshake timeout caused workers to remain WARMUP for ~90s. Manual scale requested to add 4 nodes.
oncall-eng: Manual scale started. Monitor p95/p99.
eng-runtime-lee: Manual scale complete. Immediate p99 drop observed from 4.8s -> 2.1s, p95 back near baseline. KV-prefetch toggle being applied to warm new workers.
pm-jordan: (pm-jordan) Are enterprise customers impacted? Need to surface quickly if so.
support-maya: (support-maya) Two enterprise customers flagged: ACME Inc and BetaCorp reported degraded latency. Account teams notified.
eng-runtime-lee: Short-term mitigation: enabling KV-prefetch and increasing warmup concurrency: `gcwarmup --concurrency 8` on newly provisioned workers.
ops-rita: Also bumping autoscaler handshake timeout 30s -> 90s to avoid premature aborts of warmup flows.
sre-alex: Caution — increasing handshake timeout can delay failure detection and slow global failover. Monitoring backlog closely.
oncall-eng: Action items: 1) Observe metrics for 15m, 2) Postmortem owner = eng-runtime-lee, 3) Support to notify customers and CS to prepare comms.
pm-jordan: I'll draft a short customer note with interim mitigation and ETA for postmortem.
support-maya: Filed/update tickets and added interim mitigation notes. Will escalate any critical customer replies.
eng-runtime-lee: Root-cause hypothesis: correlated burst of heavy-context chat + embedding calls triggered autoscaler to provision but model coldstart (disk read heavy) led to sequential warmup stalls; subset of hosts showed elevated disk IO causing queue to pile up.
sre-alex: Telemetry shows sustained IO wait on 3 hosts; RAID controller logged recoverable errors earlier — ops to inspect hardware.
ops-rita: Flagging affected hosts for replacement. Spinning new hosts and draining the old ones from the pool.
oncall-eng: p99 now ~1.9s, p95 ~0.9s; queue depth trending down. Keeping live coordination open for 20m. Good work.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated at 2850001800 by oncall-eng. Please add a postmortem when available.
eng-runtime-lee: Will own postmortem. Initial summary: "Provisioning warmup stall due to correlated disk IO contention + autoscaler handshake timeout mismatch." Mitigations to include preheat strategy, warmup concurrency defaults, autoscaler handshake robustness, and hardware replacement.
pm-jordan: Add product action: evaluate reserved capacity offering for high-burst customers to guarantee latency under load.
support-maya: Customers notified; will close from support side after postmortem publish.
oncall-eng: Closing coordination thread. If regression occurs, reopen this thread. :thumbsup:
